statement: The normal equations are the system of linear equations (\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X})\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{y} (equivalently expressed in gradient form as (\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})^{\top}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}) whose solution \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = \operatorname{arg\,min}_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} S(\boldsymbol{\beta}) minimizes the sum of squared residuals objective function S(\boldsymbol{\beta}) = \|\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta}\|^2 = (\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta})^{\operatorname{T}}(\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta}). The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation of this result (the derivation via quadratic form differentiation of S(b) is omitted in the source as '[proof]'), so the normal equations are stated here as a definition.

symbols.meaning: vector of observed dependent variable values (regressand)
coefficient vector of the least-squares hyperplane / OLS estimator
sum of squared residuals objective function
number of regressors plus one (including intercept)
moment matrix of regressand by regressors

properties.property: When \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X} is invertible, the coefficient vector has the explicit solution \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = (\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{y}.
properties.why: multiplying both sides of the normal equations by the inverse Gram matrix (\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X})^{-1}

properties.property: The normal equations possess a unique solution if and only if the p columns of \mathbf{X} are linearly independent.
properties.why: linear independence of the columns ensures that the Gram matrix \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X} is non-singular and invertible

properties.property: The residual vector \mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{ eta}} is orthogonal to the column space of \mathbf{X}.
properties.why: the normal equations can be written as (\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{ eta}})^{\top}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}, ensuring the dot product with any vector in the column space is zero

properties.property: The predicted values satisfy \hat{\mathbf{y}} = \mathbf{X}\hat{\boldsymbol{ eta}} = \mathbf{P}\mathbf{y}, where \mathbf{P} = \mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}} is the orthogonal projection matrix onto the space spanned by the columns of \mathbf{X}.
The matrix (\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}} appearing in the solution is the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse matrix of \mathbf{X}.
properties.why: it maps the dependent variable vector \mathbf{y} directly to the least-squares parameter estimator \hat{\boldsymbol{ eta}}

assumptions.assumption: The p columns of the matrix \mathbf{X} are linearly independent (no perfect multicollinearity).
assumptions.breaks_when: There is perfect multicollinearity between explanatory variables, causing the Gram matrix \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X} to have no inverse.

assumptions.assumption: The number of observations n is greater than or equal to the number of parameters p (overdetermined system, n >= p).
assumptions.breaks_when: The number of parameters exceeds the number of observations (p > n), which forces the columns of \mathbf{X} to be linearly dependent.

failure_modes.signature: The matrix \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X} is singular (non-invertible) and has no unique solution via matrix inversion.
failure_modes.cause: One or more columns of \mathbf{X} are exact linear combinations of other columns.

failure_modes.signature: Degrees of freedom n - p is negative or undefined, and \mathbf{X}^{\operatorname{T}}\mathbf{X} is rank-deficient.
failure_modes.cause: Sample size n is strictly less than the number of regression parameters p.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so normal_equations is recorded as a definition
